summary.intent: Explore protocol hardening opportunities (idempotency, ACID patterns) in cipher-box v1.1 while preserving or improving privacy, with focus on the IPNS write-share mechanism.
summary.outcome: Identified that IPNS write authorization is fully cryptographic (key possession), not server-enforced — enabling full social-graph blinding as a small protocol change rather than a redesign. Captured 1 architectural note, 1 forward-looking seed, and 5 high-severity bug todos, all committed to a docs branch.

repo: IPNS write control is cryptographic: a write-share recipient gets an ECIES-wrapped IPNS private key; producing a validly-signed record IS the authorization — the server is not in the trust path.

`findActiveWriteShare` is DB-row routing, not a security boundary: it redirects Bob's publish onto Alice's canonical row keyed by (userId, ipnsName); the resolve path keys by ipnsName alone and ignores the edge entirely.
The server self-increments the IPNS sequence number instead of reading it from the signed record, and never verifies the Ed25519 signature — acknowledged in a comment at ipns.service.ts:543.
The social-graph write-share edge is a caching/routing convenience; revoking a write-share requires rotating the IPNS key (which the existing rotation path already does), not edge deletion.
There is an existing todo at .planning/todos/pending/2026-02-22-crdt-ipns-inbox-sharing.md for a CRDT IPNS inbox for serverless share discovery — the new finding makes that todo's scope smaller.
`POST /ipfs/unpin` has no ownership check — any authenticated user can unpin any CID.
The quota decrement function `recordUnpin` in vault.service.ts has zero callers, so storage usage grows monotonically until lockout.
FUSE `release()` returns OK to the OS and then zeroizes/deletes the temp file before completing the remote commit — a crash after ack causes silent permanent data loss.
FUSE `mkdir` never queues the parent for republish on macOS, causing the folder to vanish on restart.
The SDK 409 retry handler re-resolves only the sequence and republishes stale children, silently overwriting a concurrent writer.

code.finding: Server optionally checks that publicKey derives to ipnsName but never verifies the Ed25519 signature on publish.
Write-share lookup redirects Bob's publish onto Alice's canonical row — this is routing, not authorization.
Server self-increments the sequence number instead of reading it from the signed record — root of sequence-divergence bug.
getFolderIpns keys the canonical row by (userId, ipnsName) on the write path.
Resolve path keys by ipnsName alone and never consults the share edge.
POST /ipfs/unpin missing ownership check — any authenticated user can unpin any CID.
recordUnpin has zero callers — quota is never decremented on unpin.
release() returns OK to OS then zeroizes/deletes temp file before remote commit completes — crash window causes silent permanent data loss.
mkdir never queues parent for republish on macOS; folder disappears on restart. Line number flagged as unverified — needs grep before fixing.
409 retry re-resolves only the sequence and republishes stale children, silently overwriting a concurrent writer.

workflow: When an agent's architectural summary conflicts with the user's mental model of the code, read the actual source before restating — the agent's framing of 'write-shares need structural exposure' was wrong and the user caught it immediately.
GSD explore sessions benefit from cross-linking new notes/seeds to pre-existing todos rather than creating duplicate artifacts.
Staging only the new exploration artifacts by explicit pathspec (not `git add .`) preserved pre-existing staged changes in the working tree.

friction: Initial agent sweep produced an incorrect architectural claim (write-share graph must be exposed for authorization) that required correcting via direct code reading after the user challenged it.
An AskUserQuestion call interrupted the flow before the corrected analysis was fully formed, leading to a slightly disjointed exchange.
